packet.headline_seed: Hundreds arrested in France after wild Champions League celebrations
packet.description_seed: Thousands of officers tried to quell unrest as crowds of fans - some firing flares - celebrated PSG's victory over Arsenal.

what: Hundreds arrested in France after wild Champions League celebrations

clean_source_blocks.text: Clashes between football fans and police across France have led to more than 400 arrests following the victory of Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in the Champions League final against Arsenal. Thousands of officers were deployed to curb unrest that disrupted bus, train and rail services in the capital Paris. Fireworks and flares were set off, while several police officers were injured in the fray. Police fired tear gas to disperse crowds in the city centre. While it marked a consecutive victory for PSG, it was also the second year in a row of football-fuelled violence, after the French side's 2025 win sparked celebrations that turned deadly. Footage from Paris appears to show flares being set off, electric bikes burning on roads and revellers smashing the glass of at least one shopfront.
Thousands of officers tried to quell unrest as crowds of fans - some firing flares - celebrated PSG's victory over Arsenal.

Riots have been commonplace in Paris and elsewhere in France in recent years. When PSG won the Champions League last year, police made more than 500 arrests across France. A man in his 20s was killed in Paris when his scooter was hit by a car during PSG celebrations. Paris police arrested 148 people after fans clashed with officers and smashed cars and store windows after the club lost the 2020 final to Bayern. When PSG won the French title in 2013 — ending a wait of 19 years — celebrations were cut short on Monday following violent scenes in which fans fought with riot police for several hours, leaving 30 people injured.

The Champs-Élysées was swarmed by fans shortly after the French team won in a penalty shootout. Earlier in the day there were clashes between police and supporters who showed up to watch the final on giant screens at PSG's Parc des Princes. Police said six vehicles, two businesses and a bus shelter were damaged during the unrest. France's interior ministry said 416 were arrested in the early hours of Sunday, including 280 people in Paris. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said seven officers had been injured and called the unrest "absolutely unacceptable". Far-right leader Marine Le Pen wrote on X: "Only in France does a football club's victory spark riots." "Only in France does everyone feel compelled to lock themselves in their homes on the evening of a victory to avoid being confronted with violence," she said.

More than 500 people were arrested by police during the Champions League final celebrations in France, and two people were reported dead and 192 injured, the interior ministry said as further festivities were planned on Sunday.

Wild celebrations erupted across the French capital and beyond on Saturday night after Paris St Germain crushed Italian opponents Inter Milan to win the Champions League for the first time.

The interior ministry's provisional assessment on Sunday morning was that 559 people had been arrested, including 491 in Paris, which led to 320 people being placed in police custody, 254 of them in Paris.

There was one fatal accident when a young man in his twenties died in a collision with a vehicle, police chief Laurent Nunez told reporters, while in the southwestern city of Dax, a 17-year-old died from stab wounds, French media reported.

payload.title: Yli 400 pidätettiin Ranskassa PSG:n mestaruusjuhlien jälkeen
payload.summary: Ranskassa pidätettiin yli 400 ihmistä sen jälkeen, kun Paris Saint-Germainin Mestarien liigan voittoa Arsenalista seuranneet juhlat muuttuivat paikoin levottomuuksiksi. Pariisissa poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua väkijoukkojen hajottamiseen.
payload.content:
Ranskassa on pidätetty 416 ihmistä Paris Saint-Germainin Mestarien liigan voittoa seuranneiden levottomuuksien jälkeen. Ranskan sisäministeriön mukaan pidätyksistä 280 tehtiin Pariisissa varhain sunnuntaina, kun juhlinta levisi kaduille ja johti yhteenottoihin poliisin kanssa.

## Juhlat muuttuivat levottomuuksiksi

PSG:n voitto Arsenalista Mestarien liigan loppuottelussa keräsi suuria väkijoukkoja Pariisiin. Champs-Élysées täyttyi kannattajista pian sen jälkeen, kun ranskalaisseura oli voittanut ottelun rangaistuspotkukilpailussa.

Viranomaisten mukaan tuhansia poliiseja oli komennettu hillitsemään levottomuuksia. Kaupungissa ammuttiin ilotulitteita ja soihtuja, ja poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua hajottaakseen väkijoukkoja keskustassa. Levottomuudet häiritsivät myös liikennettä, mukaan lukien bussi-, juna- ja raideliikenne Pariisissa.

Poliisin mukaan kuusi ajoneuvoa, kaksi liikettä ja yksi bussikatos vahingoittuivat. Kuvamateriaali Pariisista näytti muun muassa palavia sähköpyöriä kaduilla sekä rikkoutuneen liikkeen ikkunan. Aiemmin päivällä poliisin ja kannattajien välillä oli ollut yhteenottoja myös PSG:n Parc des Princes -stadionin lähellä, jonne ihmisiä oli kokoontunut seuraamaan finaalia suurilta näytöiltä.

## Sisäministeri tuomitsi väkivallan

Ranskan sisäministeri Laurent Nuñez sanoi seitsemän poliisin loukkaantuneen ja kuvasi levottomuuksia täysin hyväksymättömiksi. Pidätysten suuri määrä korostaa viranomaisten vaikeuksia hallita massajuhlintaa, joka muuttui osassa kaupunkia väkivaltaiseksi.

PSG:n mestaruusjuhliin on liittynyt vakavia järjestyshäiriöitä myös aiemmin. Kun seura voitti Mestarien liigan edellisenä vuonna, poliisi teki eri puolilla Ranskaa yli 500 pidätystä, ja yksi noin 20-vuotias mies kuoli Pariisissa skootterinsa jouduttua auton töytäisemäksi juhlinnan aikana.

Myös aiemmat PSG:n suuret ottelut ja mestaruudet ovat johtaneet väkivaltaisiin kohtauksiin. Vuonna 2020 poliisi pidätti Pariisissa 148 ihmistä seuran hävittyä Mestarien liigan finaalin Bayern Münchenille, kun kannattajat ottivat yhteen poliisin kanssa sekä rikkoivat autoja ja liikkeiden ikkunoita. Vuonna 2013 PSG:n Ranskan mestaruuden juhlat keskeytyivät väkivaltaisuuksien vuoksi, ja kymmeniä ihmisiä loukkaantui.
summary_bullets: Ranskassa pidätettiin 416 ihmistä PSG:n Mestarien liigan voiton jälkeisissä levottomuuksissa.
Pariisissa tehtiin 280 pidätystä, ja poliisi käytti kyynelkaasua väkijoukkojen hajottamiseen.
Viranomaisten mukaan seitsemän poliisia loukkaantui ja useita ajoneuvoja sekä liikkeitä vahingoittui.

Footage from Paris appears to show flares being set off, electric bikes burning on roads and revellers smashing the glass of at least one shopfront.

Thousands of officers tried to quell unrest as crowds of fans - some firing flares - celebrated PSG's victory over Arsenal.

Riots have been commonplace in Paris and elsewhere in France in recent years. When PSG won the Champions League last year, police made more than 500 arrests across France. A man in his 20s was killed in Paris when his scooter was hit by a car during PSG celebrations. Paris police arrested 148 people after fans clashed with officers and smashed cars and store windows after the club lost the 2020 final to Bayern. When PSG won the French title in 2013 — ending a wait of 19 years — celebrations were cut short on Monday following violent scenes in which fans fought with riot police for several hours, leaving 30 people injured.

The Champs-Élysées was swarmed by fans shortly after the French team won in a penalty shootout. Earlier in the day there were clashes between police and supporters who showed up to watch the final on giant screens at PSG's Parc des Princes. Police said six vehicles, two businesses and a bus shelter were damaged during the unrest. France's interior ministry said 416 were arrested in the early hours of Sunday, including 280 people in Paris. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said seven officers had been injured and called the unrest "absolutely unacceptable". Far-right leader Marine Le Pen wrote on X: "Only in France does a football club's victory spark riots." "Only in France does everyone feel compelled to lock themselves in their homes on the evening of a victory to avoid being confronted with violence," she said.
